## 4. The linear loss exponent is unavoidable

Twirling an accepted pair preserves its Bell fidelity. Its hashing yield is at least
\[
1-h_2(1-F_{\rm raw})-(1-F_{\rm raw})\log_2 3
\ge0.18500461.
\]
This is the established Bell-diagonal hashing formula of Bennett, DiVincenzo, Smolin and Wootters, §3.2.3. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}

Hence the explicit lower bound is
\[
\boxed{
Q_{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal N_{\eta,T})
\ge0.17\,e^{-\mu}sq\mu D\,\eta.
}
\tag{14}
\]

For the converse, the probability that the **entire collected output** is nonvacuum is
\[
\pi=1-e^{-\eta\gamma T},
\]
independent of the input. I obtain
\[
\boxed{
Q_{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal N_{\eta,T})
\le
\min\{1,\log_2(1+6\pi)\}
\le\frac{6\gamma T}{\ln2}\eta.
}
\tag{15}
\]

Here is the essential derivation, including the infinite optical output space. Split the normalized Choi state into vacuum and nonvacuum output blocks:
\[
J=
\begin{pmatrix}
aI_2&X\\
X^\dagger&B
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
a=(1-\pi)/2,\quad \operatorname{Tr}B=\pi.
\]
The Schur complement gives \(X^\dagger X\le aB\). After transposing the reference qubit, the cross block becomes \(Y\), with
\[
\|Y\|_2^2=\|X\|_2^2\le a\pi.
\]
Set \(C=Y^\dagger Y/a\), so \(\operatorname{Tr}C\le\pi\). Also,
\[
\operatorname{Tr}(B^\Gamma)_-\le\pi/2,
\]
because partial transposition on a qubit increases trace norm by at most a factor two.

Thus \(J^\Gamma=P-Q\) with \(P,Q\ge0\) and
\[
\operatorname{Tr}Q\le3\pi/2,\qquad
2\operatorname{Tr}_{\rm out}(P+Q)\le(1+6\pi)I.
\]
The corresponding completely positive domination gives
\[
\|T_{\rm out}\circ\mathcal N_{\eta,T}\|_\diamond\le1+6\pi.
\]
Under arbitrary adaptive two-way classical communication, \(n\) channel uses can therefore produce a \(d\)-dimensional Bell target with overlap at most
\[
F_n\le\frac{(1+6\pi)^n}{d}.
\]
This is a strong converse. The transposition-bound framework is established; the vacuum-structure estimate above supplies the particular loss bound. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"}

+\rho_{11}|-\alpha\rangle\langle-\alpha|,
\]
